Author: Prem Narayan Singh
Bench: Prem Narayan Singh
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
 Cra No. 1702 of 2020
 (Kalu Vs The State Of Madhya Prade
 Dated : 12-11-2024
 Shri Faisal Khan - advocate for the appellant.
 Shri H.S.Rathore appearing on behalf of Advocate Genera
 1.
Heard on I.A. No.9581/2024, which is an application filed under Section 430 of Bnss (389 of
Cr.P.C) for suspension of sentence on behalf of appellant.

entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Indore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. The appellant has convicted under Sections 376 of Ipc and sentenced to undergo 10 years with
fine & default stipulations.

3.  Learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the in the present case, the appellant has already completed 06 years of his incarceration out of 10 years hence, on the basis of custody period, the applicant is entitled to be released on bail.

In support of his contention, he has placed reliance over the judgment of Hob'ble Apex Court in the case of (1996) 6 SCC 731 (Supreme Court Legal Aid Committee Representing Undertrial Prisoners vs. Union of India and Others and on the order dated 10.012024 passed in CRA No.6609/2023 by co-ordinate Bench of this Court, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court as well as this Court has suspended the sentence of the accused after completion of sentence of 50%.
4.

entities.text: (1996) 6 SCC 731 (Supreme Court Legal Aid Committee Representing Undertrial Prisoners vs. Union of India and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer and prayed for dismissal of the application for suspension of sentence by submitting that in the present case, the appellant has committed rape upon her mother and in such type of heinous crime, no suspension should be granted to the appellant.

5. Having gone through the record and contention of the appellant, this Court 2 CRA-1702-2020 revealed that the conviction has been passed by learned trial court with regard to the offence of rape against mother itself.

Therefore, looking to the heinousness of the offence, no benefit of suspension Kalu vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 12 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/31229297/
1 can be granted to the appellant.
